newsitem.title: ZIMBABWE: ZIMBABWE MONEY RATES EDGE UP IN SHORT MARKET.
newsitem.headline: ZIMBABWE MONEY RATES EDGE UP IN SHORT MARKET.

text.p: Short-term trading rates on Zimbabwe's money market were quoted firmer on the back of a cash shortage on Wednesday, dealers said.
They added that, since the shortage was expected to prevail with no maturities during the day to add liquidity, the central Reserve Bank had not come into the market with a treasury bill auction.
Discount houses were selling the central bank paper in the secondary market at 16.40 percent, up from Tuesday's 16.35 percent while call money edged up to 18.50 percent from 16.25.
Rates for NCDs maturing after 30, 60 and 90 days were also quoted firmer at 19 and 18 percent (buying and selling respectively) from 17.25 and 17 percent.
Bankers acceptance bills were being bought at 17.75 percent, up from 17 percent while their selling rate edged half a percent point higher to 17 percent from 16.50 percent.
Figures from the Reserve Bank showed the market closed with a Z$138 million deficit on Tuesday from a shortage of Z$44 million on Monday.
